Catch Up with the World This Week is a 45-minute program hosted by Gavin Lee, in which he and four international correspondents examine seven days of global developments. The episode covers Spain's snap election; presidential plotting reportedly taking place over lunch at the Brasserie Concorde in Paris; Ukraine-related discussions involving Kushner and what has been described as a 'Kremlin Trap'; and an open question about Iran regarding which side time favors.

The panel for this week includes New World Magazine columnist Emma-Kate Symonds, The New York Times' Ukraine correspondent Constant Méheut, Daily Telegraph Foreign Editor Venetia Rainer, who also hosts the program Iran: The Latest, and France 24's Spain-based correspondent Sarah Morris. Production was handled by Alessandro Xenos, Rhea Smircic, Guillaume Gougeon, and Laura Burloux.

The reported items are framed as topics shaping global affairs rather than verified conclusions; for instance, the Paris lunch is described as presidential plotting without further detail on its participants or outcome, and Iran's situation is posed as an unresolved question about timing. The program presents these stories alongside one another to provide context behind current headlines.
items.title: Spain's Snap Election and Global Affairs Roundup on Catch Up with the World This Week

items.summary:
Bablu Jadhav, president of the Bharatiya Kisan Evam Mazdoor Sena (A), has alleged irregularities and corruption in the implementation of Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister's Dairy Plus Scheme across all four development blocks of Indore district. Citing right-to-information information and field verification, he asked the deputy director of the animal husbandry department to investigate the matter.

Jadhav reported that buffaloes purchased under the scheme were registered in the names of Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe beneficiaries but found tied at the homes of other influential people, while several beneficiaries reportedly did not have animals at their own residences. He also raised concerns about alleged manipulation of mobile numbers in official records and multiple family members receiving benefits.

The organisation questioned the department's response, noting that more than a month had passed since the complaint was submitted without concrete action. It has demanded physical verification of all beneficiaries, scrutiny of animal purchases, payments, insurance, tagging and mobile number records, recovery of misused government funds, and action against those found guilty.
items.title: Farmers' Organisation Alleges Corruption in Indore Dairy Plus Scheme

items.summary:
Forest officials spotted an ailing male leopard struggling to walk in the Gobratal beat of Manpur buffer forest circle during routine patrolling at Bandhavgarh Tiger Reserve. The tiger reserve's management team launched a search operation after receiving information about the animal, and field director Anupam Sahay oversaw its rescue following tranquillisation.

The rescued leopard was between one-and-a-half and two years old and has been shifted to a treatment facility for monitoring. Veterinary doctor Rajesh Tomar treated the animal while under constant observation, and biological samples were collected and sent to Nanaji Deshmukh Veterinary University in Jabalpur for laboratory examination. Further action will be taken once the lab report on the vital samples is received.

In separate news from Madhya Pradesh's Panna Tiger Reserve, forest officials detained five villagers in connection with the poaching of a tigress and are interrogating them. Dog squads deployed by the forest department and police reached revenue land in Manki village, raising suspicion that the tigress died in the revenue area and its body was thrown into the north forest area of Panna. Forest officials have intensified patrolling amid these developments.
items.title: Ailing Leopard Rescued From Bandhavgarh Tiger Reserve for Treatment

items.summary:
The Tunisian League for Human Rights condemned the conditions in Tunisia's prisons on Friday, stating that 30 inmates have died since early summer, which has been described as the country's hottest season on record. Bassem Trifi, head of the league, called the situation 'inhumane and catastrophic,' citing overcrowding and a lack of healthcare among contributing factors.

Tunisian Justice Minister Leila Jaffel acknowledged in a parliamentary address that some prisons are overcrowded and confirmed there have been 'some deaths' among prisoners. She maintained that all deceased inmates had chronic illnesses and died in hospitals rather than in prison, though Trifi argued the location of death was irrelevant since every prisoner remained under justice ministry custody.

The league previously reported 23 documented detention deaths over summer based on information from doctors, relatives, and lawyers, and is now formally demanding clarification around all 30 cases. A family member whose brother died in detention said her family had not yet received the autopsy report and wanted to know how he died.

Tunisia's weather authority attributed this year's extreme heat partly to climate change, noting intense and prolonged heatwaves with July and August as particularly severe. The highest recorded temperature reached 49.7 degrees Celsius in Kairouan in mid-July, while frequent power outages disrupted electric water pumps and compounded a shortage of bottled water.
items.title: Tunisia rights group denounces prison deaths amid heatwave

The second entry features an interview with economist Lars Peter Hansen. A third offering is a behavioral cost of living index authored by Hubert Wu, who posts on the job market from Oxford. Item five covers Luis Garicano writing about messy jobs for the New York Times.
items.title: Friday assorted links roundup

items.summary:
International Jaguar Day has been observed every November 29 since 2018 to raise awareness of threats facing jaguars (Panthera onca) across the Americas. The species once ranged over roughly 19 million square kilometers, from the southwestern United States to central Argentina, but its range has now shrunk by more than half to about 9 million km². Most surviving jaguars live in a core stronghold spanning the Amazon Rainforest and extending into the Pantanal wetlands, Chaco dry forest, and Llanos grasslands of Colombia and Venezuela.

Recent observations suggest jaguars are persisting at the edges of their historical territory beyond these central areas. In Brazil's eastern Atlantic Forest and Caatinga, fewer than 250 adult jaguars remain, prompting researchers to begin banking their genes for potential cloning efforts. At the northern range edge, a male nicknamed Cinco appeared on camera in southern Arizona in late 2025 as the fifth jaguar recorded there in 15 years.

In Honduras's Sierra del Merendón mountains, camera traps captured a young male at about 2,200 meters for the first time in a decade. Allison Devlin of Panthera noted that this high-elevation movement demonstrates how resilient the animals are, while Marcio Martinez described it as reaffirming dispersed northern populations and noting the range forms a corridor between Honduras and Guatemala.

Separately, Honduran authorities raided a businessman's home in Olancho and seized an estimated one-year-old female jaguar along with other wildlife. The animal is thought to have been captured in the Mosquitia forests stronghold and now resides at a rehabilitation center run by the Honduran armed forces, where it may be returned to a protected area if deemed fit.
items.title: International Jaguar Day Highlights Range Decline and Resilient Populations

items.summary:
Volvo Construction Equipment has delivered four customer A40 Electric articulated haul trucks to BMJV, a joint venture between Bouygues Travaux Publics and J Murphy & Sons, marking the first deliveries of this model in the UK. The vehicles are being used on the Lower Thames Crossing project, where they will move material at scale as zero-emission machines. Volvo CE had earlier become the world's first to bring an all-electric 40 ton class articulated haul truck into regular series production earlier this year (ev1).

Shaun Pidcock, Lower Thames Crossing Programme Director at BMJV, said the electric trucks show that even heavy jobs can be done cleanly and benefit those working near or living around sites. The Lower Thames Crossing is approximately 14.3 miles long (ev2) and includes more than 2.5 miles of tunnels beneath the River Thames (ev3). Once finished it will connect Kent and Essex, nearly double road capacity on London's east side, and become Britain's first major infrastructure program completed with carbon-neutral construction.

Because grid power is unavailable at the site, BMJV charges the A40s using fuel cell generators fueled by British-manufactured green hydrogen. The A40 Electric has a 40 ton (39 tonne) payload capacity (ev5), and its loaded hauler's 350 kW electric motor delivers roughly 200,000 lb-ft of at-the-wheel torque (ev7, ev9). Power comes from a 540 kWh lithium-ion battery good for up to six hours of continuous operation (ev10), with regenerative braking often extending the range to a full day's shift. Operators can also plug into a 350 kW DC fast charger at Circle K locations to charge from 10% to 90% in about an hour (ev11, ev12-ev13).
items.title: Volvo Delivers First UK A40 Electric Haul Trucks for Lower Thames Crossing

items.summary:
European leaders left a Brussels summit without an agreement on the bloc's seven-year multitrillion-euro budget, with negotiations breaking down late Thursday night and no attempt made to resume discussions on the planned second day. The center of the dispute was four countries — Denmark, Sweden, Belgium and Austria — which staged a walkout demanding a reduced budget, while Hungarian Prime Minister Peter Magyar dismissed the summit as 'completely unnecessary' and blamed European Council President Antonio Costa for convening it.

The talks centered on Germany's demand that all member states approve an additional €45 billion ($49 billion) support loan for Ukraine through 2027; Hungary, Czechia, Bulgaria and Slovakia opposed the proposal. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said 'hundreds of billions' still need to be slashed from the European Commission's original proposal of approximately €1.786 trillion, which had already been reduced by €204 billion (down 10.2%), and Costa told leaders he was planning cuts between €220 billion and €230 billion in his next proposal.

The budget is rebalancing spending: agriculture, fisheries and cohesion fall from 59.1% to 42.4%, while economic competitiveness, security and defense rise from 17.7% to 27.7%. Germany's contribution amounts to around 25% of the whole budget.

The proposal also includes a controversial EU-wide digital tax on online advertising revenues, marketplaces and user data monetization at 3%, estimated to bring in €5 billion per year — an idea originally put forward by French President Emmanuel Macron. Ireland opposes it because US tech companies have European headquarters there; Irish Prime Minister Micheal Martin warned the tax sends 'all the wrong messages.'

Some capitals fear losing the EU's triple-A credit rating without its own revenue, given around €860 billion in outstanding debts from pandemic recovery and Ukraine support. Bruegel's Jacob Funk Kirkegaard noted net contributing countries like Germany are more open to a national-contribution financing model because higher interest costs would fall on them.

Experts say there is no cause for alarm yet: the self-imposed deadline is before the end of 2026, and leaders will return in late December hoping for a better atmosphere. The 'Sensible Seven' — Germany plus six other net contributors who pay more than they receive — back Berlin's reduction push against 17 member states led by France and Italy that insist the budget should grow.
items.title: EU budget talks collapse after tense Brussels summit

UN Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs Tom Fletcher said Friday he is 'appalled' by the fatal attack on an aid worker in Upper Nile State, South Sudan. Writing on X, Fletcher called on all parties to ensure humanitarian staff can work safely and offered condolences to the victim's family.

Fletcher warned that 42 humanitarians have been killed in the country since January, a figure he attributed as reported speech from his own statement. Humanitarian agency GOAL Global confirmed Thursday that one of its staff members died in the incident, describing the attack as 'unacceptable' and urging authorities to investigate.

Neither GOAL Global nor UN officials identified the victim or specified who carried out the assault. The article provides background context rather than attributing these facts directly: South Sudan gained independence from Sudan in 2011, civil war broke out in 2013 after a power struggle between Kiir and his then-deputy Riek Machar, and a 2018 peace agreement laid the groundwork for a transitional unity government. Tensions reportedly escalated again in March 2025 when Machar was placed under house arrest, where he remains on trial on charges including treason and murder that he denies.

The item is dated 27 November 2026 with an update of the same date.
items.title: UN relief chief appalled by aid worker killing in South Sudan

items.summary:
Family members of five people killed in a fuel tanker accident and local residents gathered outside Al Salam Mosque in Cairo's Waraq district on Friday to say goodbye to the deceased. Among those who died were five members of one family: a father, his daughter, his son, and two nephews.

The crash involving a fuel tanker sparked a massive fire on Cairo's Ring Road on Wednesday, Egyptian authorities said, killing at least 31 people (ev1) and injuring at least 21 others (ev2). The blaze occurred on the highway encircling the capital in Waraq, a densely populated neighborhood in Giza within Greater Cairo. Rescue workers pulled people from burning vehicles as more than two dozen cars and motorcycles were left charred, according to the Health Ministry.

The incident comes amid Egypt's broader toll of fatal traffic accidents each year, which officials attribute to speeding, poor road conditions, and weak enforcement of traffic laws. In January alone, 21 people (ev3) were killed and 16 injured (ev4) in a multi-vehicle pileup on a road near the southern province of Beni Suef.
items.title: Cairo mourns 31 victims of deadly fuel tanker inferno as families bid farewell

items.summary:
Ancient rainforests in Malaysian Borneo hold a form of wealth distinct from the monetary gains produced by industries such as logging and palm oil. For the Indigenous communities that call these forests, rivers, and mountains home, the landscapes provide food, medicine, and livelihoods while preserving generations of knowledge, traditions, and culture through their interconnected ecosystems.

As industrial pressures continue to intensify on these environments, some communities are working harder than ever to defend their homes. In doing so, they aim to protect the ecological wealth that exists within these forests.
items.title: Indigenous Communities Defend Borneo's Ancient Rainforests

items.summary:
Survey researchers at UMass Amherst argue that widespread voter opposition to artificial intelligence infrastructure contributed to the Democratic gains in the 2026 midterm elections. The authors note that ballot measures limiting data centre construction were approved by voters in 40 of 41 instances, citing examples from California, Kansas and North Dakota alongside a battery storage ban in Kansas, a moratorium in Maine and an outright ban in Ohio.

Drawing on an August 2026 survey of 1,000 American adults, the researchers report that 65% of respondents oppose building data centres locally. That opposition is bipartisan: 76% of Democrats, 67% of independents and 52% of Republicans expressed it. Open-ended responses attributed concerns to environmental impact (cited by 28%), quality-of-life effects such as noise at 15%, higher utility costs at 10% and general distrust of AI at 13%. One respondent described water depletion, another cited doubled electricity prices.

The authors contend that Republican ties to the unpopular industry hurt them politically. They note President Donald Trump voiced strong support for data centres before Election Day but observed that many Republican congressional candidates distanced themselves from unrestricted construction as local backlash grew through 2026, while Democrats made opposition a campaign theme. Among those opposing data centres, 48% said they would back the Democratic House candidate versus 25% for the Republican; among voters in states holding Senate races, 47% planned to vote Democratic and 28% Republican.

The researchers conclude that even after accounting for partisanship, ideology and demographics, opposition to data centres was associated with support for Democrats. They suggest this gives elected Democrats an incentive to place AI regulation on their legislative agenda, while noting popular resistance is unlikely to fade soon.
items.title: US midterms: Anger over data centres may have helped Democrats

visual.alt: Bar chart. Democrats: 76% opposed 76 %; Independents: 67% opposed 67 %; Republicans: 52% opposed 52 %.

items.summary: Two companies named 2026 Best Places to Work in the Power Industry have very different histories. Babcock & Wilcox (B&W), founded in 1867, is an established firm with about 1,650 employees worldwide that entered through its Akron, Ohio headquarters of 471 employees at survey time. BrilliT, a wholly owned subsidiary of Rappahannock Electric Cooperative formed as an IT firm in 2022 inside the cooperative, has just 31 employees and is the only company to have won both in 2025 and again this year.
items.title: Babcock & Wilcox and BrilliT Named 2026 Best Places to Work in the Power Industry

items.summary:
The pCloud Pass password manager suffered a cyberattack that the company says was quickly contained, with users reporting unknown devices connecting to their accounts even while two-factor authentication remained enabled. Customers in two Reddit threads reported receiving notifications about an unfamiliar device named 'pd' linking from IP address 45.131.244.7 in Luxembourg, which they say belongs to pCloud's own infrastructure; some recipients had no unfamiliar devices listed when checking their accounts, and others received the alerts despite never using the password manager or having requested deletion of an associated storage email nearly a year earlier.

pCloud stated that only a small number of user email addresses were exposed during login attempts, which triggered its automatic notification system, while passwords, notes, and other stored data remained uncompromised because it is encrypted on customers' devices. The company did not disclose whether any encrypted password vaults were accessed or stolen, even though such theft would let attackers crack them offline without facing the service's login rate limits or two-factor protections; this risk was demonstrated in the 2022 LastPass breach, when attackers stole backups containing encrypted vaults and later linked to cryptocurrency thefts from cracked weak or reused master passwords. A reader also noted that an 'Open settings' link in the notifications pointed to passqa1.pcloud.com, which appears to be a quality assurance environment rather than production.

In its statement pCloud warned customers about phishing attempts and said it would never request their master passwords or recovery words over email, phone, or chat. The incident is part of a broader wave of password manager attacks this month: earlier in November mSeven Software advised mSecure users to change stored passwords, reset two-factor authentication, and remove passkeys after an encrypted customer database was reportedly stolen, and on Wednesday 1Password disclosed a breach caused by a threat actor who compromised an employee's GitHub account and deployed malicious code to its backend services while reporting that password vaults and their encryption keys were not compromised. The article also includes promotional content for Adaptive Security's AI agents, which analyze email intent, context, and behavior to detect phishing, business email compromise, and invoice fraud through a 14-day read-only scan of Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace with no MX changes.
items.title: pCloud Confirms Password Manager Hack After Suspicious Login Alerts

items.summary:
According to updated International Energy Statistics, global electricity generation reached 31.8 trillion kWh in 2025, more than twice the 15.1 trillion kWh recorded in 2000 (ev1). Renewable energy became the largest source of global power for the first time in 2025, accounting for 34% of generation compared with 33% from coal (ev5), while renewable output rose from 2.9 trillion kWh in 2000 to 10.6 trillion kWh in 2025 and coal-fired output increased by 83% between 2000 and 2024, reaching 10.5 trillion kWh (ev7). Coal's share of the global mix has fallen from a peak of 41% in 2007 to its current level below renewables' share (ev6).

China remained the world's largest generator with 10.7 trillion kWh, more than one-third of the global total and up at an average annual rate of 9% since generation stood at 1.4 trillion kWh in 2000; coal supplied more than half of China's electricity while renewables contributed over one-third (ev15). The United States produced 4.5 trillion kWh, with natural gas accounting for 40%, renewables 26%, and nuclear 17% (ev20), after growth slowed to less than 1% annually between 2000 and 2020 before expanding by 2% a year from 2020 to 2025, driven partly by commercial demand including data centres. India generated 2.1 trillion kWh, around 70% of it from coal (ev23), with output more than tripling between 2000 and 2025 at an average annual growth of 5%, attributed to population growth and manufacturing expansion.

Together China, the United States, and India produced 17.3 trillion kWh in 2025, exceeding the combined output of all other countries (ev16). The figures highlight both the scale of global electricity demand growth and a changing generation mix, with renewables now providing the largest share worldwide.
items.title: Renewables Overtake Coal in Global Power Generation

visual.alt: Bar chart. Renewables (34%) 34 %; Coal (33%) 33 %; Natural gas (40%) 40 %.

items.summary:
Coweta County voters will decide in a January 12 special election whether to repeal the rezoning for Project Sail, a $17 billion data center campus on more than 800 rural acres about 45 miles southwest of Atlanta that county commissioners approved 3-2 in April. Probate Judge Carrie B. Markham ordered the election Monday after opponents filed their petition Oct. 16 under Georgia's Home Rule provision, submitting 14,820 signatures and clearing the required threshold by 94 votes once elections officials verified 11,065 of them against a base of 109,703 active electors.

The ballot question reaches well past one project: besides repealing the April 7 rezoning, it would strip data centers from the county's zoning code and ban data centers and cryptocurrency mining operations in every zoning district. Atlas Development objected to the petition on Oct. 23, but Markham threw out that objection the same day she called the election, finding under Georgia Supreme Court precedent no party has legal standing to object to a Home Rule petition.

The state's high court opened that door last year when it ruled unanimously that a McIntosh County zoning ordinance was subject to the same referendum procedure Coweta's opponents used. Atlas filings with the Georgia Department of Community Affairs describe 13 buildings of about 378,000 square feet each plus substations, finished by the end of 2036 and worth $17,161,900,000 at build-out, drawing water demand of 9.1 million gallons a day with 3.03 million gallons a day of sewage and 800 tons of solid waste a year.

Prologis, the San Francisco-based industrial REIT under contract to take over the project, said in October that the petition does not change its commitment to Project Sail, noting JC Witt described the site as chosen partly for its closeness to Georgia Power's Plant Yates. Atlas first projected more than $1 billion a year in local taxes, though Prologis's latest projection is about $100 million a year while state filings list $163 million.

Commissioners Alphonso Smith, Jeff Fisher and John Reidelbach voted for the rezoning, which moved about 829 acres near Sargent and Wagers Mill roads from Rural Conservation to Industrial. A group of residents sued in May in Coweta County Superior Court to void it, alleging commissioners ignored the land's conservation designation and its role in groundwater recharge; that case is pending.

If Coweta's measure passes on Jan. 12, no data center or crypto mine could be zoned anywhere in the county. Georgia Power has been seizing homes and easements across Coweta and Fayette counties for a 35-mile, 500-kilovolt line to feed AI data centers, while voters elsewhere this month rejected 41 local measures in ten states almost unanimously against the data centers.
items.title: Coweta County Voters to Decide Fate of $17 Billion Data Center Megaproject

items.summary:
Medical device company Boston Scientific is notifying individuals affected by a cyberattack that exposed cloud-based applications and data between May 7 and May 1, with the breach determined to have occurred on November 5. According to a notification sample shared with U.S. authorities, hackers used social engineering in a voice phishing attack to access the firm's cloud infrastructure; the company became aware of unauthorized access on May 12. The incident exposed information from 117,789 people across multiple states, including full names, physical addresses, Social Security Numbers, government-issued ID numbers, medical and health insurance information, and dates of birth.

Boston Scientific stated that patient medical records and data from remote monitoring systems, connected devices, clinical case management applications, manufacturing, ordering, distribution, or service were not exposed. The company reported no disruption to operations, product safety, or performance, contained the incident with outside cybersecurity experts, notified law enforcement, but did not offer free credit monitoring—instead recommending that affected individuals use free credit reports and consider fraud alerts or credit freezes.

The breach is described as a second cybersecurity incident in 2026. On August 25 of this year, Boston Scientific disclosed an earlier cyberattack that caused network outages and global operational disruption to order processing and shipping; CrowdStrike's investigation found the attacker breached an internet-facing device but no evidence they compromised cloud applications. A spokesperson confirmed the recent breach is unrelated to the August intrusion and declined further details.

Boston Scientific is a Massachusetts-based manufacturer of stents, catheters, pacemakers, defibrillators, and endoscopes with more than 59,000 employees, 13 manufacturing facilities, and operations in 127 countries. The company reported more than $20 billion in revenue in 2025.
items.title: Boston Scientific Data Breach Exposes Personal and Medical Information

items.summary:
The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) has introduced a revised framework permitting foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) to participate in physically settled non-agricultural commodity derivatives, including non-agricultural commodity derivative contracts excluding options on goods and related indices. Previously, FPIs could trade only cash-settled non-agricultural commodity derivative contracts and corresponding indices within the commodity derivatives segment of recognised stock exchanges.

The rules take effect on June 1, 2027, following stakeholder representations, deliberations by the Commodity Derivatives Advisory Committee (CDAC), and public consultation. For non-cash settled non-agricultural commodity derivatives, Sebi has barred FPIs from taking fresh positions that increase their existing holdings in an expiring futures contract from three trading days (T-3) before the tender or staggered delivery period begins, though positions arising from the expiry devolvement of options on futures are exempt. Clearing members must also stop accepting or clearing trades that raise an FPI's open position in the near-month deliverable futures contract starting at T-3.

Voluntary square-off or rollover by close of market hours on the day prior to the tender period (T-1) remains the primary exit route for FPIs. Any residual open positions at the end of T-1 will automatically devolve post-market hours, before clearing corporation end-of-day activities, onto the proprietary account of a designated Trading Member (TM) or Trading Cum Clearing Member (TCM) at the exchange's declared closing or daily settlement price. Agreements may include a pre-agreed, disclosed 'Risk Absorption Charge' payable by the FPI to the designated TM/TCM on devolvement, alongside any service fee, while exchanges and clearing corporations will standardise onboarding agreements and notify post-closure window guidelines.
items.title: Sebi Expands FPI Access to Physically Settled Non-Agri Commodity Derivatives

items.summary:
Brent crude futures rose 0.8% to $97.30 a barrel on Friday, reaching their highest level since November 9, while US WTI crude gained 2.6% to $85.85 a barrel compared with Wednesday's close, according to Reuters; there was no settlement for WTI on Thursday due to the US Thanksgiving holiday.

The rally followed several sessions of gains driven by fresh attacks on energy infrastructure and commercial shipping in the Middle East. Yemen's Houthi militants claimed responsibility for strikes on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery, one of the kingdom's largest refining facilities and a major crude export hub, along with other Saudi targets. Separately, Saudi Arabia's Jazan refinery temporarily suspended some operations after a projectile struck the facility Thursday, killing a worker and injuring several others, according to the kingdom's Energy Ministry.

The Strait of Hormuz has also come under pressure as Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two tankers exploded and caught fire after striking sea mines near Oman's Khasab port while attempting to cross the waterway. However, expectations of ample global supplies continue to limit price upside; Brent remains well below its earlier levels despite the rebound, with the International Energy Agency flagging a possible fourth-quarter supply surplus.

US crude inventories rose by 1.1 million barrels to 418.9 million barrels in the week ended November 20, according to the Energy Information Administration, though the increase was smaller than analysts' expectations of a 1.5-million-barrel build. Investors now focus on Sunday's OPEC+ meeting, where member countries are expected to review production policy for 2027 and likely maintain existing output targets through at least the first quarter of next year.

Oil prices will depend on whether these geopolitical developments translate into sustained supply disruptions or remain largely a risk premium in futures markets.
items.title: Crude Prices Rise as West Asia Attacks Revive Supply Fears Ahead of OPEC+ Meeting

visual.alt: Bar chart. Brent crude futures gain 0.8 %; WTI crude futures gain 2.6 %.

items.summary:
Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Friday (Nov 27) in Kuala Lumpur that Malaysia's lawsuits against Google over alleged failures to address harmful online content will not affect the US tech giant's investments in the country. The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission sued Google for US$146 million on Wednesday, prompting concerns about whether the case would disrupt plans to invest billions of dollars in data centres and other infrastructure.

Anwar defended the legal action, saying Google had been slow to respond to complaints, with some left unanswered for up to half a year. He cited cases of online gambling that were reported but saw no action taken after six months. The MCMC alleges that YouTube failed to adequately address online gambling, scams and fraud on its platform and did not take proactive action against harmful content published by a controversial local blogger.

Google announced this month plans to invest US$15 billion in Malaysia over the next two years to build data centres and other infrastructure, expanding on a US$2 billion investment disclosed in 2024. The country is Southeast Asia's fastest-growing hub for new data centres, which house servers that train and run AI tools such as chatbots and image generators.

Anwar said he had spoken with Google's President and Chief Investment Officer Ruth Porat on Thursday, reporting that she told him Google would cooperate to address the issues. Malaysia has previously taken action against other major social media platforms, including TikTok, over allegations they failed to remove content deemed 'grossly offensive.'
items.title: Malaysian PM Says Lawsuits Won't Deter Google Investments

items.summary:
OpenAI filed counterclaims against Apple on Friday in federal court in San Jose, California, accusing the iPhone maker of pressuring suppliers to avoid its devices and using unfair employment agreements to keep talent from leaving. The filing also alleges that Apple stole OpenAI's trade secrets, turning an earlier lawsuit brought by Apple into a two-way dispute over intellectual property between the companies.

The legal conflict has overshadowed OpenAI's separate bid to sell its own products, which would place it in direct competition with Apple. Former Apple design leader Jony Ive is helping develop this product line, beginning with what is expected to be a doughnut-shaped smart speaker.
items.title: OpenAI Accuses Apple of Pressuring Suppliers and Stealing Trade Secrets

items.summary:
The Intellectual Property Office of Singapore ruled in November that Real Madrid and Barcelona lost their joint bid to trademark 'El Clasico', with the decision favouring Liga Nacional de Fútbol Profesional. Principal assistant registrar Mark Lim Fung Chian noted the unusual alignment, observing that clubs who are fierce rivals on the pitch were united against the league's governing body. The ruling found that El Clasico was well known in Singapore as a commercially organised and promoted sporting property associated with La Liga rather than merely describing matches between the two clubs.

The dispute centred on an application filed in August 2022 featuring both club crests, a stylised 'C', and the words 'EL CLASICO' across goods including video game software, clothing, footwear, entertainment, sporting activities, and ticket reservation. La Liga opposed it in June 2024 with evidence of viewership figures ranging from 27,165 for a December 23, 2017 match to 68,384 for an October 28, 2018 match, plus two other matches drawing 56,361 in April 2021 and 60,521 in October 2021. The adjudicator gave limited weight to the clubs' evidence because it largely concerned use outside Singapore.

La Liga also won on similarity grounds, finding that consumers might mistake the proposed mark for an official variant of its existing marks given only minor differences in accent, capitalisation, and spacing. Represented by law firm Ghows, La Liga was awarded $10,500 in costs. A procedural wrinkle emerged when the clubs' legal representatives stopped acting in August 2026, leaving them without written submissions or representation at the hearing.

The adjudicator cautioned that his findings should not constrain future adjudicators where both sides fully argue the same issue.
items.title: Real Madrid and Barcelona Lose Singapore El Clasico Trademark Fight

items.summary:
Chinese shoppers are buying budget down jackets as cold weather arrives, with products priced below 500 yuan (S$97) selling briskly while consumers question the value of premium brands. A 399 yuan down jacket filled with 90% goose down made for Peking University sold out online in mid-November after drawing attention on Chinese social media, and a women's down jacket from US brand Rokka&Rolla priced at 499.9 yuan also sold out at Walmart-owned Sam's Club.

The trend signals more cost-conscious spending in a market where people have long been pushed toward luxurious clothing. Research firm iiMedia said the average price of a down jacket more than doubled over the past decade and was forecast to exceed 1,000 yuan in 2025, yet an November survey found jackets priced between 401 yuan and 600 yuan were most popular among consumers.

Bosideng, China's largest down jacket maker, has said the average price of its core products rose to about 1,500 yuan to 2,500 yuan. Mark Tanner, founder and managing director of Shanghai-based consultancy China Skinny, said many shoppers want comparable design or function without a large prestige premium rather than the cheapest copy.

The challenge is apparent for brands moving upmarket: Bosideng launched its third collection from British designer Kim Jones in November, but some higher-priced items saw limited sales on Tmall. A blue jacket advertised with brand ambassador Wang Leehom carried a price tag of about 2,278 yuan yet sold just 16 units over the 30 days to Nov 13.

Consumers are becoming more selective rather than simply trading down: Alibaba said more than 30 million down jackets were sold during 2026's Singles' Day festival, with Uniqlo and Bosideng ranking first and second by sales. Uniqlo surpassed 100 million yuan in Tmall sales within 24 minutes of promotions launching on Oct 20.

Demand remains resilient at the top end: Canada Goose said Greater China revenue rose 32.5% in the quarter ended September, and Moncler's chief corporate and supply officer Luciano Santel described China as a healthy region for its premium outerwear brand. Tanner noted that like every luxury brand, they will need to work harder than ever to justify their price points.

The contrasting performances reflect broader divergence in Chinese consumption: as economic uncertainty weighs on middle-class households through a property slump and weak wage growth, many are trading down or demanding greater value while wealthier shoppers continue spending on products offering quality, performance or status. Lv Jiaming, a 27-year-old factory worker in Shanghai, said he would not buy another jacket costing more than 1,000 yuan because there is little difference between one priced at 500 to 600 yuan and one over 1,000 yuan unless it is exceptionally good.
items.title: China's premium puffer jacket push meets consumer resistance

items.summary:
The Central Reserve Police Force has been deployed in Tamil Nadu's Thiruparankundram Hill near Madurai to oversee security and surveillance on Saturday, following a directive from the Supreme Court that the ceremonial Karthigai Deepam lamp be lit at the Deepathoon stone pillar atop the hill. The deployment comes ahead of the scheduled lighting ceremony at the Deepathoon.

Police personnel had already been stationed in the area near the Deepathoon before the CRPF arrived to reinforce security for the event.
items.title: CRPF Deployed at Thiruparankundram Ahead of Karthigai Deepam Lighting

Foreign Secretary S Jaishankar said Friday that attacks on maritime shipping and seafarers are unacceptable and require a global response, speaking at the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA) council of ministers meeting in New Delhi. He stressed that international law, particularly the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, must be respected to address these threats.

The 25th IORA council of ministers meeting was attended by foreign ministers and heads of delegation from all 23 member-states, according to a joint communique issued after Prime Minister Narendra Modi met with them. The communique expressed concern over the undermining of maritime safety and security for vessels and seafarers and reaffirmed commitments to freedom of navigation, unimpeded commerce, peaceful dispute settlement, sovereign equality, territorial integrity, non-interference in internal affairs, peaceful co-existence, and mutual benefit.

India announced a grant of $500,000 toward the association's institutional and financial capacity-building. Jaishankar said this cooperation is needed to counter terrorism, narcotics trade, illegal unreported and unregulated fishing, climate events, and disaster situations, while noting that India chairs IORA and pursues its Mahasagar vision of mutual and holistic advancement for security and growth across regions.
items.title: EAM Jaishankar Condemns Attacks on Shipping at IORA Meeting

US equities climbed on Friday, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average gaining 361.11 points, or 0.72%, to close at 50,544.06 (ev1). The S&P 500 rose 51.78 points, or 0.74%, to 7,235.66 (ev5), while the Nasdaq Composite advanced 204.05 points, or 0.87%, to 23,789.86 (ev8). All but one S&P 500 sector traded higher, with information technology stocks providing the largest boost.

The gains came after a volatile week in which Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's return and Anthropic briefly falling below its IPO price added turbulence to AI-related names. Investors weighed buying opportunities following a steep sell-off against concerns over rising costs, heavy borrowing, and whether large AI investments will deliver sufficient returns (Reuters). David Morrison, senior market analyst at Trade Nation, told Reuters that investors viewed the pre-Friday selloff as overdone and expected steadier gains ahead.

Despite this week's turbulence, the S&P 500 and Nasdaq were on track for their best weeks since April and August respectively, with the Dow heading toward its strongest week since April 2025 (dt13). Chipmakers that had been hit hard recovered ground: Micron and Marvell each gained more than 2% (ev14), while the broader chip gauge rose 1.3% (ev15). AI-linked companies including Sandisk, Lumentum, and Dell also advanced.

Traders were pricing in a December Federal Reserve rate hike after data showed US economic growth faster than initially estimated in the third quarter and October inflation accelerating. Gold and silver miners rallied as precious-metal prices recovered; Newmont gained 3.6% (ev16) while the Global X Silver Miners ETF advanced 4% (ev17). Altria fell 1.8% (ev18) after considering an all-cash bid for Imperial Brands, and Vertex Pharmaceuticals slid nearly 10% (ev19) after the FDA extended its review of a kidney-disease drug by up to three months.

Trading volumes were thin following Thanksgiving's half-day session on Friday. Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by 3.47 to 1 on the New York Stock Exchange (ev20) and 3.15 to 1 on the Nasdaq (ev22). The S&P 500 recorded five new 52-week highs with no new lows, while the Nasdaq posted 22 new highs against 31 new lows.
items.title: US stocks rise as investors snap up beaten-down AI stocks

ZEEL's board approved a share buyback on November 12, 2026, covering up to 65,934,065 fully paid-up equity shares of Rs 1 face value each. The offer represents about 6.86% of the company's total paid-up equity capital as of March 31, 2026.

Because the buyback size falls within 10% of paid-up equity capital and free reserves under both standalone (7.22%) and consolidated (6.61%) audited financials for FY26, shareholder approval was not required. The company is executing the offer through a tender route via a special stock exchange acquisition window, with BSE as designated exchange, Emkay Global Financial Services Limited as manager and company broker, and MUFG Intime India Private Limited as registrar.

Shareholders holding shares worth up to Rs 2,00,000 based on the NSE closing price of Rs 67.21 on the record date qualify for small-shareholder status, with entitlement approximated at about one share per 14 held and actual rates around 7.15% in each category. About 11,241,759 shares are reserved for small shareholders while roughly 54,692,306 go to the general category.

Bid settlement and payouts or unblocking of unaccepted demat shares are scheduled by December 14, 2026, with share extinguishment set for December 21, 2026.
items.title: Zee Entertainment Launches Rs 600 Crore Share Buyback

items.summary:
Pete Edochie, celebrated for his role as Okonkwo in the 1987 television adaptation of Chinua Achebe's novel Things Fall Apart, died on 25 November at age 79 in Enugu after a prolonged battle with prostate cancer. Joy Nnamdi said he was the perfect choice to bring the character to life and described him as 'the ultimate tough man,' rarely seen laughing despite his deep voice and commanding presence that made him an enduring embodiment of patriarchal authority on screen.

Born 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Edochie studied journalism and television in the UK before joining the Eastern Nigerian Broadcasting Corporation in 1967. He joined the pro-separatist Voice of Biafra during Nigeria's civil war, describing those years as 'the greatest personal challenge' he ever faced amid hunger and hardship. He later switched to acting over a decades-long career that bridged home-video productions and global streaming platforms.

His work reached wider audiences through MultiChoice's Africa Magic channels across the continent and via Lionheart (2018), Netflix's first original Nigerian film, as well as his 2017 Ghana comedy John and John. His contributions were recognised in 2003 when he received the Member of the Order of Niger honour.

In recent years Edochie gained an unexpected online following as social media users turned his distinctive expressions into memes conveying disbelief or exasperation, introducing his work to younger Africans while some who grew up watching him recalled being scared by his occultic and villain roles. Sani Muazu said parents in Kano would invoke 'Okonkwo will come and visit you' to keep children in check.

Tributes poured in after his death from fans, fellow actors, and President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, who described the loss as significant for Nigeria's film industry and cultural heritage. Actress Genevieve Nnaji called him a 'chosen one,' while Patience Ozokwor remembered him as an elder figure of wisdom.

His son Leo Edochie said his father's most important legacies were telling the truth and remaining honest, describing him as living an exemplary life worthy of emulation. Two of his six children, Yul and Linc Edochie, followed into Nigerian film, though some of the actor's endearing moments came when he let his guard down.

In 2021 he made a brief appearance in music star Phyno's video for 'Highway,' surprising fans with dance moves that revealed a lighter, more playful side to the septuagenarian behind his formidable screen persona.
items.title: Nigeria's 'ultimate hard man' actor Pete Edochie dies aged 79

items.summary:
A documentary titled Heal offers what is described as the most intimate look yet into Princess Catherine of Wales's private life, including how her cancer affected her physically and mentally. The film will broadcast on BBC TV on Sunday (Nov 29), ahead of airings in the United States on NBC, Australia on Channel 9, and Canada on CTV and Noovo.

Catherine, 44, wife of Prince William, is shown crying as she listens to messages from her three children during a charity challenge to scale Britain's three highest peaks within 24 hours. She told her brother James Middleton that the recordings would give her 'the reason to get out of hospital' and 'finish this challenge.' The climb involved Scafell Pike in England, Ben Nevis in Scotland, and Snowdon in Wales, a feat she completed in June to raise money for The Royal Marsden Cancer Charity.

Catherine said in March 2024 that tests following major abdominal surgery had found an undisclosed form of cancer after it was revealed her father-in-law King Charles also had the disease. She is now reported to be in remission after a course of chemotherapy. In voiceovers and clips from meetings with other cancer sufferers, she described being confronted by her own mortality as 'very hard' and characterized hospital time as dark, disorientating, and frightening.

She said the project's aim was to give something back to those who cared for her while helping others navigate life with cancer. Catherine acknowledged that her story differed from others and could not reduce 'the grief and pain that so many face,' but expressed hope that viewers would be reminded they are not alone and that beauty and joy can still be found even in difficult times.
items.title: Princess Catherine's Cancer Documentary 'Heal' to Air on BBC

items.summary:
A government-funded clinic in Sweden, Mottagning Neuropsykiatri, has opened as what its doctors describe as the first facility worldwide dedicated solely to reassessing people who hold autism or ADHD diagnoses. The service is driven by young adults like Freya, 12 at referral time and now seeking a police career, whose original diagnoses they came to question once those labels became barriers to employment in Sweden's military, police, train driving and piloting roles.

Clinic lead psychologist Sebastian Lundström says the approach focuses on present-day functioning rather than past history, adding a note of reassessment without erasing the original diagnosis. He cites a small peer-reviewed study of 72 participants in which roughly 80% did not meet diagnostic criteria, while noting that all attendees already wanted to lose their diagnoses and so are unrepresentative.

Critics warn the service could deepen stigma by framing neurodiversity as something undesirable or fixable. Navid Ghannad of Autism Skåne argues these are lifelong conditions whose symptoms can resurface later in life, leaving people without support if reassessed away from their diagnosis. Advocacy figures including Jenny Hedin and Eric Donell contend the focus should be on changing employment rules rather than removing diagnoses.

The clinic is open only one day a month and serves locals; during its first year of operation some 400 to 500 people spoke with Lundström about reassessment. Requests from applicants in the UK, Denmark, Norway and Germany have been turned away as the service currently does not accept international patients.
items.title: Sweden Opens World's First ADHD and Autism Reassessment Clinic

items.summary:
At least 22 cassowaries have been killed on Queensland roads in 2026 so far, according to figures from the Department of the Environment, Tourism, Science and Innovation. That figure is almost double the between-11-and-13 road deaths recorded each year since 2022 (ev1, ev2), with dt3 confirming the reference period as 2026 and ev4, ev5 noting the prior annual range of 11 to 13. Tropical Vets director Graham Lauridsen described a cluster of fatalities earlier this year, occurring roughly one per week for about six weeks (ev1). The rise may partly reflect better reporting and a healthier population after several years without major cyclones, though Lauridsen said that is not grounds for halting protection efforts.

Cassowary advocates are pressing the state government to roll out AI road signs following what they describe as a successful trial. In July 2025 (dt7), the Department of Transport and Main Roads announced a three-month test on the Kennedy Highway at Kuranda that achieved 97 per cent accuracy in identifying birds and a 31 per cent decrease in fatal strikes, figures drawn from the department's account (ev8, ev9). Afterward, the Cassowary Recovery Team identified five road-strike hotspots for potential sign installation. Liz Gallie of Mission Beach Cassowaries said locals expected signs to be deployed next at these sites but expressed frustration that nothing has happened since; in correspondence seen by the ABC she wrote to a minister in September and received an October reply stating more trials were needed but no plans had been made, with her own words emphasizing 'we just need it at Mission Beach' (ev10).

A TMR spokesperson said investigations are ongoing into how AI signs could be incorporated into ongoing cassowary-safety work, but noted that no further funding has been allocated and no trials are planned. The government is instead continuing a community awareness program, including two static roadside billboards on the Bruce Highway near Tully and Innisfail to encourage drivers to slow down (ev1). Jax Bergersen of the Kuranda Conservation Community Nursery said everyone in the Cassowary Recovery Team was frustrated after high hopes for the signs. Lauridsen added that AI signs avoid driver complacency associated with static signage, help mitigate conservation costs, and are especially timely now that hatching season has ended and chicks are on the road.
items.title: Cassowary advocates push for AI road signs after deaths nearly double

items.summary:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is reportedly preparing to offer his election rival, Yashar chairman Gadi Eisenkot, a rotational government arrangement in which he would serve as the second prime minister. According to Channel 13 citing officials in the Prime Minister's Office, the proposal has been communicated through informal channels and Likud remains divided over its conditions.

Eisenkot is reportedly highly sceptical of Netanyahu's offer while continuing preparations to form a government before his mandate expires on 6 December. Avigdor Liberman, chairman of Yisrael Beytenu, warned that such an arrangement could be a ploy by the caretaker prime minister to derail Eisenkot's new government and drag out unity talks until he finds a pretext to break them off.

Eisenkot has pledged not to form a unity government with Netanyahu without approval from coalition partners including Democrats chairman Yair Golan and Liberman. Senior members of Eisenkot's bloc told Channel 13 that B'Yachad chairman Naftali Bennett plans to vote against an Eisenkot-led administration if it is formed before all avenues for negotiations with Netanyahu have been exhausted.

Eisenkot's four-party bloc currently holds only 48 seats, well short of the 61-seat majority required to form a government. To bridge the gap, Eisenkot has two options: relying on Arab-led parties or seeking backing from ultra-Orthodox parties such as United Torah Judaism and Ra'am.

Channel 12 reported that Ra'am offered to back the security decisions of an Eisenkot-led government throughout its proposed four-year term in return for ministerial portfolios and significant investment in Arab communities. It remains unclear whether Eisenkot will seek support from Arab parties or accept Netanyahu's offer before his mandate expires on 6 December.
items.title: Netanyahu reportedly offers Eisenkot rotating PM deal amid coalition uncertainty

items.summary:
As rain fell at the grand final, North Melbourne defeated Melbourne by 56 to 52 on Friday night (7 Nov) to complete a historic three-peat in the AFLW. The piece notes this is their third consecutive premiership and that for the first time since 2023 they lost a game during the season, with challengers coming closer than in prior years.

North Melbourne won by dominating three phases of play. In the opening quarter Tess Craven kicked the first goal within 21 seconds and captain Jasmine Garner added a second six minutes later; both came off stoppage rather than turnover as they had done against this opponent previously, with Garner recording seven disposals, four inside-50s and the goal in that term.

Melbourne then shifted to a kicking game in the second quarter, producing their only two goals of the match from intercepts while posting 39 kicks to North Melbourne's 14 handballs. The Demons recorded a pressure factor of 2.30 across that quarter before rising to 2.38 in the third term, yet North Melbourne held its lead and turned the middle quarters into an arm's-length stalemate as intercepts from Garner (eight), Ash Riddell (seven) and Amy Gavin Mangan, Jenna Bruton and Eliza Shannon (all six each) helped drop Melbourne's kick rate to 50 per cent.

A five-minute burst in the last quarter turned a six-point lead into a 26-point victory. A long rebounding kick unlocked North Melbourne's speed, leading to a stoppage inside-50 and a goal from Bella Eddey that put them up by 13 points before Blaithin Bogue added two more goals for the comprehensive win.
items.title: North Melbourne Win Historic AFLW Third Consecutive Premiership

items.summary:
Three people familiar with the matter said hackers have breached the U.S. Air Force's flagship cloud computing platform, known as Cloud One, in an intrusion that could jeopardize sensitive tactical, personnel and logistics data.

The breach was discovered within roughly a month during work to upgrade the system, according to two of those sources, and has since caused disruption across the platform. Reporters were unable to establish the identity of the attackers, determine the full scope of the intrusion, or confirm whether any data had been stolen.

In response, the Air Force issued a statement declining to comment on the security posture, vulnerabilities, or operational status of specific networks and systems, while asserting that it continuously takes prudent measures to protect Department of the Air Force information, systems and mission capabilities.
items.title: Hackers Breach U.S. Air Force Cloud One Platform

items.summary:
The purse of Se Nah Park, a 24-year-old woman swept into the ocean at Panther Beach near Santa Cruz three weeks ago, was found Wednesday by a beachgoer at 4 Mile Beach south of Panther Beach. The Santa Cruz County Sheriff's Office confirmed that Park had been caught in powerful waves on 8 November while attempting to return through the 'keyhole' archway after gathering around a bonfire with five others; four members tried to make their way back, and three reached safety up the cliffside before being struck by another wave. According to her friends' GoFundMe page, Park did not survive.

Park's body has still not been located as record high king tides affected the west coast during the discovery. The U.S. Coast Guard suspended active search efforts on 9 November after Lt. Max Holloway stated that extensive searching had exhausted available resources and environmental conditions complicated recovery attempts; his statement offered condolences to Park's family.

Despite the suspension, Park's family and friends have continued their own search efforts in the weeks since. Her supporters shared a message expressing hope 'that Senah can be found and brought home to rest,' noting that finding her purse may help bring them closer to locating her body.
items.title: Purse of California Beach Victim Found After Three Weeks

items.summary:
Schools in England are set to be required by Labour's proposed national curriculum reforms to allocate time each day for primary pupils and several days a week for secondary pupils to read for pleasure. Education Secretary Lucy Powell is expected to announce the measures, which include a statutory reading test at year 8 and an emphasis on whole books rather than excerpts, as part of efforts to tackle declining literacy rates and rising screen time. Powell told the Times that falling reading levels represent 'a ticking timebomb' for future generations while noting that reading should also be enjoyed by every child.

Powell is also expected to announce programmes of study for England's curriculum, which could include shorter exams in some GCSE subjects such as history, geography and modern foreign languages. Shadow education secretary Laura Trott welcomed the reforms but said they must accompany a serious effort to reduce classroom screen time. A July education committee inquiry recommended extending the National Year of Reading into a national decade and called for a reading guarantee ensuring all children have regular opportunities to enjoy reading.

Research cited in reporting found that reading enjoyment among UK children had fallen to its lowest level in two decades, with a sharper decline among teenage boys while girls' levels remained stable or improved. A survey by the National Literacy Trust reported that 39.1% of girls aged eight to 18 said they enjoyed reading in their free time compared with 25.7% of boys.
items.title: England Schools to Set Aside Time for Pleasure Reading

items.summary:
Sukhnidh Kaur's new book, Your Perfect Dream Girl: Influencers, AI, and the Future of Desire (Penguin Random House India), examines how online platforms shape young urban women through filters, follower counts, snark forums, dating apps, deepfakes, and AI sexbots. Structured as 25 letters to a faceless man, it combines journal entries, love letters from men she encountered growing up, testimonies, and interviews with industry insiders. Kaur argues that women have always been the most profitable product of technological revolution, contending that their consumption is essential rather than incidental to these platforms' business models.

The reviewer notes the book blends memoir and cultural commentary but becomes 'barely-explored analyses, clouded by Kaur's own privilege,' reading at times as self-indulgent babble more suited to a memoir. The writing is described as clunky and failing to support its ambition of rigorous criticism, with an overused metaphor that generalizes women as passive prey rather than highlighting structural binds. A comparison between her online commodification and young girls trafficked from Nepal was called tone-deaf for demeaning the trafficking issue.

The sharpest material comes from interviews rather than Kaur's own arguments. Her conversation with Viraj Sheth, CEO of Monk-E creator agency, offers an insider view into influencer industry economics, as does her talk with fellow influencer Divija Bhasin. Meta correspondent Pranav Dixit explains how platforms are 'reluctant' to build safeguards around data harvesting and argues that change requires a lawsuit, PR crisis, or reputational damage; the reviewer connects this to recent backlash over Meta's withdrawn generative AI feature using public images. Kaur also lists beauty products marketed to women across three pages.

The book is criticized for its central gap: despite being a successful influencer herself, Kaur hesitates to apply an interrogating eye to her own experience or industry, and she largely fails to foreground perspectives from other highly successful female influencers on the economics and compromises of influencer culture. The reviewer concludes that while the book starts an interesting conversation about how women bear technology's worst impulses, it ultimately lacks original arguments and 'the fortitude to see through the very questions it raises.'
items.title: Review Criticizes 'Your Perfect Dream Girl' for Unanswered Questions

items.summary:
Delhi's air quality index reached a hazardous level of 454 at 6:51 AM on Saturday, 28 November, according to data from AQI.in. The reading was close to the seven-day peak of 449 recorded at 6 AM on 21 November, which fell within a period that ended on 27 November with its lowest value of 170 at noon on 26 November.

Friday's air quality first improved before deteriorating sharply. The AQI dropped from 273 in the morning to 144 around 3:01 PM, then began hovering above 300 by about 7:30 PM and climbed continuously through the night, staying between 300 and 400 until midnight before rising above 400.

At 6:11 AM on Saturday, Delhi's pollutant levels were high across several measures. The PM10 level stood at 428 micrograms per cubic metre against a WHO guideline of 45 micrograms per cubic metre; carbon monoxide was reported at 3,395 ppb, nitrogen dioxide at 25 ppb, sulphur dioxide at nine ppb, and ozone at two ppb. Temperature was 25°C with humidity at 30%, wind speed at 3.6 km/h, and a UV index of 3.1.

On the national scale, AQI.in reported Bettiah in Bihar as having the worst air quality on Saturday with an AQI of 682, followed by Ghazipur at 558 and Saharsa in Bihar at 488; Srinagar also hovered in the hazardous category at 480. The two sources used different classification scales: AQI.in labels readings above 300 as 'hazardous', while PTI, citing Central Pollution Control Board data, classifies 401-500 as 'severe'.

Vehicular emissions were the largest contributor to PM2.5 pollution in real-time source apportionment estimates recorded between 1 AM and 9 AM on Friday morning, accounting for 32% of the estimated load. This was followed by biomass burning at 22.8%, secondary organic aerosols at 14%, and secondary inorganic pollutants at 12.3%. Waste burning accounted for 10.7% of the pollution load, with industrial emissions at 4.2%, mineral dust and ash at 1.8%, coal combustion at 1.5%, and mixed combustion at 0.8%. Of the 57 monitoring stations that recorded data on Friday morning, 36 were in the 'poor' category, 17 reported readings in the 'moderate' category, and four fell into the 'very poor' category; the Terminal 3 station of Indira Gandhi International Airport registered the worst city-level reading at an AQI of 346.
items.title: Delhi air quality worsened to hazardous levels on Saturday

items.summary:
PV Midhun Reddy of the Yuvajana Sramika Rythu Congress Party (YSRCP) told Hindustan Times that his party supports the proposed delimitation legislation, and he denied any alignment with the Bharatiya Janata Party. He said the support is driven by two factors: women's reservation in Parliament, which his party has backed regardless of which party holds power, and protection of Andhra Pradesh's representation through a 50% proportionate increase in seats that the Centre had assured him would be included this time.

Reddy clarified that YSRCP has long criticized the BJP over election conduct and electronic voting machines. He said his party is not focused on central politics but rather on its own state, adding that it wants to raise a concern about further regional imbalances arising from the exercise. He noted that if delimitation were based purely on population without the proportionate seat increase, Andhra Pradesh would suffer losses.

The report includes background on Pallavi Singhal, who covers agriculture and rural economy for Hindustan Times; she joined in 2019 as a trainee reporter with The Indian Express before working at Moneycontrol and Informist.
items.title: YSRCP's Midhun Reddy Backs Delimitation Bill Over Women's Reservation

items.summary:
A Hindustan Times morning brief dated November 28 rounds up developments in politics, current affairs, sports, and entertainment. The central political story concerns the government's proposed Delimitation (Second) Bill, 2026.

The bill proposes a 50 per cent increase in Lok Sabha seats for every state and Union territory to bring into effect the reservation of seats for women in Parliament and legislative assemblies, according to the bill accessed by HT. The delimitation exercise would be carried out on the basis of the last published census. In response, opposition leaders indicated that the beleaguered INDIA bloc has begun preparing a final fight against the constitutional amendment bill, with some parties asking lawmakers to reach Delhi by Sunday and the bloc considering making a public appeal to DMK chief MK Stalin.

On the international front, a report by The Jerusalem Post indicates Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is weighing an arrangement in which he would serve as second prime minister under a rotation agreement with Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot, aiming to break Israel's political deadlock. In sports news, Mumbai Indians reinstated Rohit Sharma, 39, as captain ahead of IPL 2027 after replacing Hardik Pandya.

In entertainment, the Ranbir Kapoor and Yash-starrer Ramayana became the fourth Indian film to cross ₹1000 crore domestically on day 23 of its run. The film had earlier crossed ₹500 crore within six days of release in theatres that opened November 5.
items.title: Hindustan Times morning brief covers delimitation plan, Netanyahu rotation and Ramayana box office

items.summary:
A man in Bengaluru shared on the r/BangaloreSocial subreddit how an ordinary walk home from a friend's place turned into helping an injured food delivery worker, visiting him at the hospital, then taking over his pending deliveries. The incident reportedly occurred around 11:30 am when he came across the delivery person who had met with an accident and stopped to help take him to the hospital.

Rather than leaving after the rescue, the man offered to complete the still-pending food orders even though he had no prior experience in food delivery. He described figuring out the process as he went along, then also offering to drop the worker home afterward. The two spent time talking about work and life while laughing over the unusual situation.

During their conversation the man learned that the delivery worker earned around Rs 50,000 to Rs 60,000 every month, a figure he said caught his attention but for which no further details were given. He did not disclose the worker's working hours, delivery platform, or how the monthly earnings were calculated.

The man summed up that he had left home expecting only a casual walk and instead ended at a hospital delivering food orders and dropping off a stranger, ending with a wish for the worker's recovery. The post drew appreciative reactions from Reddit users who praised his willingness to help someone he never met.
items.title: Bengaluru Man Helps Injured Delivery Worker and Completes His Pending Orders

items.summary:
Wanda Dench, a grandmother in Arizona, accidentally sent a Thanksgiving dinner invitation to 17-year-old Jamal Hinton's number in 2016. After he responded with a selfie clarifying the mistake, she welcomed him anyway, beginning a friendship that has continued for about a decade.

The project is expected to be released around Thanksgiving next year, CNN reported. Dench and Hinton are working with Lifetime's writers while also preparing for another family gathering this holiday season, which they recently discussed on a park bench in Arizona. Their plans include coordinating celebrations with their growing families and attending media interviews.

Their friendship attracted widespread attention after Hinton shared the exchange that brought them together during 2016, when the US was dealing with racial tensions, political divisions, and the aftermath of the Pulse nightclub shooting in Florida. Dench initially expected the attention to fade but said it surprised both of them that media coverage returned every year through their annual Thanksgiving celebrations.

The gatherings have not been identical each year as family circumstances changed; Lonnie, Dench's husband, died in 2020 from Covid-19 complications, and Dench was diagnosed with breast cancer in 2024 before becoming cancer-free. Hinton recently married and is putting his attention into a non-profit called Bounce Back, which aims to give young people opportunities for sports, life skills, higher education, and career options.

Hinton also hopes to use the public interest in their friendship to draw attention to challenges faced by ordinary families, noting that rising living costs have made expenses such as Thanksgiving meals and holiday travel more difficult. Although friends encourage him to post more on social media because he is an influencer, Hinton prefers to concentrate on activities outside the online world.

Dench is exploring new interests as she approaches her 70th birthday, including making quilts with other women that will be donated to cancer patients, drawing on her own chemotherapy experience. She said she wants to remain open to new friendships rather than treating age as a reason to slow down and does not have a detailed plan for the years ahead.

"I've just learned in life that you start somewhere," Dench told CNN, "and I'm just always amazed on where I end up because it's always a surprise, and so I don't have an exact plan. I'm just moving forward."
items.title: Arizona Grandmother and Stranger Turn Thanksgiving Friendship Into Lifetime Film

items.summary:
Concerns have been raised about a proposed delimitation bill, with critics suggesting it fails to resolve key issues and may widen the divide between northern and southern states. The estimated 50 percent increase in Lok Sabha seats is said to potentially expand disparities significantly while diminishing southern representation.

The bill has also sparked warnings about intra-state gerrymandering, drawing references to previous delimitation exercises in Assam and Jammu and Kashmir. Despite a 25-year freeze that addresses some proportional concerns, questions remain regarding the immediate implementation of the women's reservation quota within the current House strength. The Women's Reservation Bill itself was passed as the 106th Constitutional Amendment Act in 2023 after its journey included key milestones and multiple setbacks before parliamentary approval.

Separately, opposition leaders plan to oppose delimitation bills following a Union Cabinet decision approving key proposals including increased state representation.
items.title: Concerns over delimitation bill widening north-south gap and gerrymandering

items.summary:
The Women's Reservation Bill passed both Houses of Parliament in September 2023, becoming the 106th Constitutional Amendment Act. The bill has a long political history that traces back to Constituent Assembly debates promoting equal status rather than separate quotas for women. Significant milestones along its path include the 1974 Towards Equality report, Rajiv Gandhi's efforts toward local representation, and panchayat quotas enacted under P.V. Narasimha Rao. Despite setbacks during various governments, the bill finally cleared both legislative chambers in September 2023.

Its implementation depends on delimitation, which raises questions about when women will achieve one-third representation in Parliament and state assemblies. Separately, Chandrababu Naidu and H D Kumaraswamy backed the Delimitation Bill and women's reservation, advocating for enhanced political representation in southern states. Meanwhile, opposition leaders plan to oppose delimitation bills after the Union Cabinet approved key proposals including increased state representation.
items.title: Women's Reservation Bill Passes as 106th Constitutional Amendment

items.summary:
Ranbir Kapoor's mythological epic Ramayana: Part 1 reached a net collection of Rs1,000 crore in India on day 23 of its theatrical run, even though daily collections had fallen below Rs10 crore at that point. The film also stars Yash and Sai Pallavi.

Despite the slowdown, Ramayana overtook Baahubali 2's lifetime worldwide collection as reported by trade figures. Its global gross is now stated to have hit Rs1,790 crore, prompting questions about whether it can catch up to Dhurandhar 2, described as the only other Bollywood film to reach this milestone in 2026.
items.title: Ramayana crosses Rs1,000 crore as Ranbir Kapoor film eyes Dhurandhar 2 lifetime
