President Droupadi Murmu has recommended the Delimitation Second Bill 2026 for consideration by the Lok Sabha, following its approval by the Union Cabinet. The formal presidential sanction permits the bill's introduction during a special session of the Lok Sabha scheduled for November 30. That session is intended to gauge whether the National Democratic Alliance retains sufficient support and enough numbers to pass the legislation.

Bharat Rashtra Samithi has expressed backing for the delimitation bill, citing its role in securing southern parliamentary representation and strengthening treasury benches toward a majority in the Rajya Sabha. Separately, security measures were heightened at Tirupparankundram hill ahead of the Karthigai Deepam festival, with the deployment of CRPF and Rapid Action Force personnel.

Retired judges have been overseeing temple operations after the Supreme Court suspended the temple trust board, while authorities maintain a buffer zone and monitor the ceremony amid political and community responses. In other developments, Kolkata Police sealed the entrance to Trinamool Congress headquarters under construction over safety concerns and deployed additional forces, and Elementary Teacher Training teachers demonstrated in Chandigarh demanding full salaries and protesting corruption linked to job allocations.
items.title: President Murmu Forwards Delimitation Second Bill 2026 to Lok Sabha

items.summary:
Transport Minister C P John said on Saturday that the Kerala government plans to set up road safety councils at local body levels and promote grassroots road clubs as part of efforts to reduce accidents in the state. He described a two-pronged 'enlighten and enforce' approach under the Jeeva-Suyathra Mission, combining public education with strict enforcement against traffic rule violators.

John said accident-prone locations are now being identified using a grid system that divides the country into one-km-by-one-km squares, supported by around six to seven lakh volunteers from organisations including the National Cadet Corps and police cadets. He noted speed limits would continue varying by road type rather than undergo blanket revision, citing 70 kmph on a six-lane highway as an example.

On KSRTC operations during the Sabarimala pilgrimage season, John said 461 buses were operating exclusively for pilgrims and that 110 old damaged buses had been refurbished. He added MLAs had contributed 110 buses to support the corporation, with a mayor expected to provide one more.

John also addressed reports of cyber fraudsters using fake traffic challans, saying he had informed police to initiate legal action though incidents were not widespread. On delays in appointing board and corporation chairpersons, he said discussions within the UDF were underway and hoped the process would complete soon.
items.title: Kerala Transport Minister John Outlines Road Safety Councils

items.summary:
The Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam announced on Saturday that it would support the delimitation bill, which proposes increasing Lok Sabha seats in all states by 50 percent. The DMK passed this resolution at a meeting chaired by party chief MK Stalin, stating that the change 'will protect Tamil Nadu's representation.' Party leader A Raja said after the meeting that the party's consistent demand is that its seat share of 7.18 percent should not be altered, and he was quoted saying procedural issues would be addressed with an amendment if necessary.

The bill will be introduced by the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance government in Parliament during a special session beginning Monday, after the Union Cabinet cleared it on Friday. The legislation maintains the current proportion of seats based on the 1971 census and freezes the arrangement for another 25 years until 2051.

The DMK had previously opposed the bill while part of the Opposition INDIA bloc but is now supporting it, a shift that comes as its relationship with Congress has strained after Congress extended support to the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam-led government in Tamil Nadu. The party still holds 22 members in the Lok Sabha and eight in the Rajya Sabha.

The bill requires a two-thirds majority of votes in Parliament to pass, which the ruling NDA does not have in either House, so it needs Opposition support. It had failed to secure that majority when introduced as the 2026 Constitution 131st Amendment Bill during an April special session. The Nationalist Congress Party faction led by Sharad Pawar also announced its support after the Cabinet cleared the bill on Friday; it has eight Lok Sabha MPs and one Rajya Sabha member, though it had voted against the bill in April.

The Opposition INDIA bloc contends that delimitation could upset the political balance between states and give BJP an electoral advantage through gerrymandering. A Raja noted that Stalin previously said there was no question of compromise on the exercise, even as the party raised concerns about its possible adverse effects.
items.title: DMK Announces Support for Delimitation Bill

items.summary: Türkiye's National Defense Ministry reported on Saturday that students from the Libyan Naval Academy completed practical training aboard the Turkish Navy frigate TCG Turgutreis, which is operating as part of the Turkish Naval Task Group. The ministry stated via its NSosyal platform that the sessions took place in port under coordination by the Homs Joint Maritime Training Centre Command and that certificates were presented to students upon completion. The post also included photographs documenting the training.
items.title: Turkish Frigate Trains Libyan Naval Academy Students

items.summary:
The Supreme Court permitted a one-time ritual of lighting a ceremonial lamp at a disputed stone pillar on Thirupparankundram hill, but the November 20 order did not resolve the underlying religious and legal dispute over the pillar's identity, history, or access to the contested site near the Sikandar Badusha Dargah. The BJP and Sangh Parivar have recast this limited interim measure as a broader Hindu triumph, with leaders describing it as 'the Ayodhya of the South' and Prime Minister Narendra Modi invoking Lord Murugan.

The Court's November 27 response to non-compliance by State and temple authorities escalated significantly: it directed that the lamp be lit on November 28, issued contempt notices to officials, suspended the temple board of trustees, appointed two former High Court judges as receivers, deployed CRPF personnel, permitted devotees to light lamps at least 50 metres from the Dargah (ev1), and vacated its earlier stay of relevant High Court findings. The article raises questions about whether such extensive intervention in a religious institution's administration was proportionate.

The BJP's Assembly strength reportedly fell from four MLAs to one in the 2026 election, yet the party frames the controversy as serving a national campaign ahead of northern State elections (dt2). The proximity of the Hindu temple and Muslim place of worship is presented as an opportunity for broader contestation over religious identity. The article also criticizes media language that describes the disputed structure simply as 'Deepathoon,' suggesting this risks settling its character in public perception before it is settled in law, while noting the Court referred to it only as a pillar identified as Deepathoon.

The piece concludes that when political mobilization, judicial intervention, and media language reinforce one another, an unproven claim can acquire the appearance of an established right. It argues disputes must be resolved based on evidence, law, and custom rather than political pressure, warning against using the lamp to mobilize one community against another.
items.title: Supreme Court's One-Time Lamp Order Recast as Hindu Political Victory

items.summary:
On Friday, Binance announced it received in-principle approval from Bhutan's Gelephu Central Bank to establish regulated digital-asset operations at the Gelephu Mindfulness City hub. The exchange described this as a first step rather than a full license, noting that Binance must satisfy conditions set by the central bank before any regulated activities can begin. This development is part of plans to expand into five Asian markets next year.

Binance's Asia-Pacific head SB Seker told Reuters earlier in the week that the company holds ongoing conversations with at least five or six markets, three of which are in mature stages, though he did not name them specifically. Binance currently operates licenses in 15 markets and has identified South and Southeast Asia as key priorities.

The partnership will include an operational presence involving local hiring and investment in digital assets. Seker characterized the move as a strategic decision reflecting commitment to operating within clear regulatory frameworks. This expansion push follows a security breach that US authorities have linked to North Korea, which resulted in $6.3 billion being stolen from Binance's platform last month and halted withdrawals for two days; the company reported finishing work to recover its withdrawal systems.

Binance stated it could cover losses tied to the October cyberattack without raising fresh funds.
items.title: Binance Receives Preliminary Approval to Establish Asia Hub in Bhutan

items.summary:
Russian President Vladimir Putin took part in a flag-raising ceremony for the country's newest nuclear-powered submarine, the Perm, held in Severodvinsk on Friday. The Perm is described as the fifth Yasen-M class submarine to join Russia's fleet over six years.

Putin stated that Russia was among the few countries capable of building such powerful nuclear-powered submarines. He also announced that five missile-carrying submarines are scheduled to be delivered to the Navy by 2030, including three Yasen-M class vessels.
items.title: Putin Unveils Russia's Newest Nuclear-Powered Submarine

Security measures have been intensified at Tirupparankundram hill in preparation for the Karthigai Deepam ceremony, with CRPF and Rapid Action Force personnel deployed alongside additional troops to maintain order. Two retired judges are overseeing temple activities following the Supreme Court's suspension of the temple trust board, and contempt notices were issued to key officials due to non-compliance with judicial orders.

Devotees have participated in prayers and ceremonially lit the Deepam under strict supervision, while a buffer zone has been established around the nearby dargah. Political and community leaders have responded to the ruling, with continued dialogue ongoing on jurisdiction and religious concerns.

items.summary:
Health ministry data show that babies born to Japanese nationals in Japan during the first half of 2026 rose by 1,379 from a year earlier to reach 320,458, marking the first increase in births since 2015.

The rise may reflect higher marriage numbers in 2024 after years of decline during the COVID-19 pandemic, though marriages themselves fell by 708 to 229,458 in January-June. A preliminary count including Japanese nationals born abroad and foreign nationals born in Japan showed births up to September declined 0.3% to 523,304, leaving a ministry official unable to say whether the full-year figure will rise or fall.

By prefecture, Tokyo led with 41,745 births (up 1,864), followed by Osaka at 25,431 (up 292), Kanagawa at 23,961 (up 122), Aichi at 21,325 (up 392), Saitama at 18,489 (up 88), Chiba at 15,946 (up 121), and Fukuoka at 15,294 (up 308). Births grew in 24 of the country's 47 prefectures, with rises concentrated in urban areas. Tottori recorded the lowest figure at 1,383 (up seven), while Akita fell by 45 to 1,402 and Ishikawa, Niigata, and Tochigi posted large declines of 416, 330, and 258 respectively.

The annual number of births has fallen since 1975, dropping below 1 million in 2016 and below 700,000 in 2024. In 2025 the figure reached 671,270, a record low for the 10th consecutive year, with the decline progressing about 15 years faster than forecasts from the National Institute of Population and Social Security Research. The government is attempting to slow the trend through measures such as expanding child allowances.
items.title: Japan births rise for first time in 11 years

On Friday, Uganda launched Africa's first clinical trial of an experimental mRNA vaccine against the Bundibugyo species of the Ebola virus. The State-run Uganda Virus Research Institute said the trial was being conducted in collaboration with Moderna, which manufactures the inoculation. There are currently no shots for this less common strain, which is behind the current outbreak in neighbouring Democratic Republic of Congo that has become the second-largest on record.

mRNA vaccines give cells temporary instructions to make a harmless piece of a germ, training a person's immune system to recognise and fight it later. This Ugandan trial was the second for the jab after Moderna tested it in Canada in August on adults aged 18 to 65; the new study will test safety and immune response in children one year and above.

Moderna's vaccine is also set to enter trials in DRC soon, alongside another Bundibugyo-targeting vaccine developed jointly by the University of Oxford and the Serum Institute of India. Vaccine Alliance Gavi said on Friday it had signed a purchase agreement for 1.5 million doses (ev1) of the ChAdOx1 candidate.

After the Covid-19 pandemic, Gavi set up a $50 million First Response Fund (ev2) to buy doses in advance even before they are fully tested. It said it would have them ready for deployment should trials prove successful and be approved by the World Health Organization and the DRC government.

The WHO says the outbreak in Congo has caused more than 5,700 confirmed deaths out of more than 11,000 cases (ev3) since being declared in May. Pratyay Saikia, a 25-year-old from Haryana who was studying food technology in 2022 when he saw an advertisement from the recruitment agency Magic Billion, is now working as a butcher at Metzgerei Lederer in southern Germany after completing a three-year apprenticeship. He arrived in Baden-Württemberg with about 180 other Indians to do an Ausbildung program, joining a group of Indian workers subject to social security contributions in Germany that has grown sevenfold over the past decade to more than 140,000 professionals.

Germany is facing a shrinking and aging population and needs skilled electricians, mechatronics technicians, solar panel installers, truck drivers as well as software specialists and nurses. A 2024 study by the Bertelsmann Foundation concluded that Germany requires about 288,000 foreign skilled workers per year until 2040 to fill shortages left by retiring workers, while a report from FMC Group noted more than 369,000 skilled job positions went unfilled in 2025. Despite this need, many firms, particularly the Mittelstand small and medium-sized enterprises, are hesitant to recruit from India because hiring Indian electricians is relatively new for them.

Daniel Raja, managing director of NM NextMittelstand GmbH, said German companies often overlook young talent abroad and do not actively recruit internationally, while high language requirements keep many skilled positions unfilled. Saikia studied German to the B1 level but found it insufficient at work; his co-workers helped him improve over a year. David Kipp, researcher in the Global Issues Research Group at SWP, said he is skeptical about lowering language requirements because limited language knowledge makes exploitation easier by reducing contact with German institutions.

Raja added that workers' councils sometimes resist hiring from abroad on the mistaken belief that cheap Indian labor will take jobs or undercut wages. He uses unconventional outreach such as TikTok Live sessions to engage employers and dispel concerns. Germany has traditionally relied on Central and Eastern European workers, but studies show those workers are increasingly reluctant to relocate because of better opportunities at home.

Pia Fallstrom, ELA spokesperson, said the European Labour Authority's 2025 study found that posted third-country nationals are increasing mainly in construction and transport. Kipp noted Indian recruiters exploit a Vander Elst visa mobility loophole by obtaining residence permits in CEE states before posting workers to German sites under it. While regulations protect posted workers, ELA said the practice has often led to wage-dumping through complex subcontracting arrangements, letterbox companies, bogus self-employment and other non-compliance.

Raja reported cases of recruitment scams where families took loans for a promised job in Germany only to end up doing manual labor elsewhere. Saikia stressed verifying that a recruitment agency is legitimate by checking its detailed website and the CEO's willingness to speak early on. Kipp argued prevention requires streamlining migration procedures, expanding pre-departure cultural training, identifying trusted entities and combating social media scams.
items.title: Indian workers fill Germany's labor gaps but face hurdles and risks

The author responds to a prompt asking whether discussions of strong-AI disempowerment offer detailed comparisons with how such systems might empower humans, and whether any analysis addresses the 'net empowerment effect.' The author's impression from searching the literature is that systematic analysis of this net effect remains surprisingly underdeveloped relative to the volume of work on disempowerment. The main example cited by Bentham's Bulldog and John Halstead largely argues against the likelihood of net disempowerment, while a GPT answer reportedly recognizes that establishing powerful AI does not establish human disempowerment.

The author repeats the general claim that critiques of strong-AI disempowerment are long on emotion and short on social science, marginal thinking, and comparative analysis. The author adds that much of what currently limits human agency is dependence on other people who possess scarce cognitive abilities rather than an absence of one's own cognitive capacities. Many disempowerment scenarios also assume AI capabilities will keep improving while the technologies humans use to control, monitor, bargain with, and direct those AIs remain comparatively static, a default assumption the author questions.

The strongest counterargument identified is that empowerment might be temporary and revocable whereas eventual disempowerment might be irreversible; this asymmetry deserves serious consideration but still requires explicit modeling rather than simply counting delegated decisions. The author also notes that many assumptions producing AI disempowerment, such as mental laziness, similarly produce disempowerment from growing wealth at a slower pace, and suggests the marginal increase in disempowerment may not be large over the longer term.

The author references remarks by Seb Krier as characteristically excellent but does not elaborate on their specific content.
items.title: Author Argues Net Empowerment Effects of Strong AI Remain Underdeveloped

Taiwan held local elections on Saturday across its 22 cities and counties, choosing mayors, council members, and other local leaders who will serve four-year terms. Taiwanese authorities accused Beijing of attempting to interfere in the vote and sow distrust in the electoral system, allegations that Chinese authorities rejected.

Polls opened at 8am and closed at 4pm, with counting underway as results were expected within the day. Taipei incumbent Mayor Chiang Wan-an of the opposition Kuomintang was leading against Puma Shen of the ruling Democratic Progressive Party, which had not won the capital's mayorship since 1994. Neither camp claimed victory or conceded defeat.

Taiwanese officials warned voters to be vigilant about fake claims on social media amid alleged Chinese disinformation efforts. Taiwan's ministry of national defence counted some 33 sorties from China's People's Liberation Army warplanes between Friday and Saturday, including bombers and fighter jets flying toward the island. In 2022, the DPP won in only five out of 22 localities.

Unlike presidential elections where relations with Beijing are central, this vote focused more on local concerns such as social welfare benefits affecting daily life. President Lai Ching-te campaigned for DPP candidates, appearing Thursday night to support his party's mayoral candidate in Taoyuan City.
items.title: Taiwan Holds Local Elections Amid China Interference Accusations

The ASEAN Centre for Energy (ACE) projects that data centres will account for about 20.7% of Southeast Asia's additional power demand between 2025 and 2030, driven by the expansion of artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and digital services. Muhammad Rizki Kresnawan, a senior officer at ACE for Energy Modeling and Policy Planning, noted that data centres have distinct electricity consumption patterns unlike conventional commercial or industrial buildings because their demand is shaped by digital infrastructure growth rather than typical building factors.

The projection relies on ACE's ASEAN Coordinated Transition Scenario (ACTS) model, which emphasizes the need for stronger regional power interconnection to support industry electrification and transport alongside data centre expansion. Kresnawan also flagged that uncertainty around AI development makes it difficult to forecast future demand accurately, complicating governments' ability to assess private sector requests for large volumes of clean electricity and water.

ACE Executive Director Razib Dawood said the ACTS model estimates the ASEAN Power Grid will require average annual investments of about US$405 billion, with cumulative investment reaching US$14.1 trillion by 2060. The scenario assumes accelerated energy efficiency gains, electrification, and coordinated fuel switching among member states.

ACE is promoting multilateral electricity trading arrangements involving three or four countries to improve regional power sharing, while the Brunei-Indonesia-Malaysia-Philippines Power Integration Project (BIMP-PIP) continues facing implementation challenges. Indonesia signed a memorandum of understanding in July to explore exports to Singapore, but the initiative remains uncertain after its senior energy minister said the country was not yet ready and prioritized domestic needs.

ACE warned that without stronger policy measures and investment, total regional energy consumption could rise from about 480 million tonnes of oil equivalent (Mtoe) in 2025 to 2,047 Mtoe by 2060. Separately, a May 2025 report by Ember estimated data centres could account for roughly one-third of electricity consumption within the information and communication technology sector, equating to about 360 terawatt-hours.
items.title: Data Centers To Account For 20.7% Of ASEAN Power Demand Growth By 2030

Residents of Guinea-Bissau reacted with mixed emotions to Thursday's announcement that presidential and legislative elections, originally scheduled for next month, have been postponed until November 2028. Some citizens expressed frustration at the military government delaying polls intended to mark a return to civilian rule following last year's coup; resident Mamadu Dabó Junior criticized the decision as undemocratic, arguing governance instruments must be submitted to the people before decisions are taken. Fellow resident Jalica Cante described the postponement as 'a bit tricky' given the country's current situation and warned it is difficult for Guinea-Bissau to remain unable to move forward. Bissau trader Muahmede Nhabali said residents do not know why the polls, due on 6 December, were postponed while markets are at a standstill, and appealed to military command that elections should not be held as late as November 2028.

Transitional president General Horta N'Tam defended the decision Thursday, stating conditions were not in place to hold credible elections next month due to insufficient technical, material, and financial resources. The military had previously promised a one-year transition to civilian rule after last year's coup; an August constitutional referendum replaced the semi-parliamentary structure with strengthened presidential powers, though opposition groups called for a boycott of that vote. Elections are now scheduled for 26 November 2028, exactly three years after the generals came to power.

The country has experienced four previous coups and attempted coups since gaining independence from Portugal in 1974.
items.title: Guinea-Bissau Postpones Elections Until 2028
